prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: מערכת שעות כיתת י'2 – סמסטר א' (language he, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "ראשון" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שני" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שלישי" spans 1 col × 3 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "יום" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
  col 2: header "שעה" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 89px
  col 3: header "מקצוע" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 63px
  col 4: header "מורה" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 68px
  col 5: header "חדר" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 76px
  col 6: header "הערות" · longest unbreakable word 64px · one-line width 700px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A Hebrew RTL class timetable for grade י'2, semester א', used to find when a lesson occurs, who teaches it, where it meets, and any special instructions.","reading":"Readers scan from the right: first the merged day block, then the time, then subject/teacher/room as the lesson identity, and finally the notes as exceptions or instructions. Day rowspans group consecutive lessons, so those blocks must remain visually coherent.","groups":["יום + שעה — temporal anchors read first and define each rowspan block","מקצוע + מורה + חדר — the lesson's identity and location, compared across rows","הערות — secondary free-text annotations that can absorb wrapping"],"keep_intact":["time ranges such as 08:15–09:00","day labels ראשון, שני, שלישי","subject names","teacher names at least at word level","room numbers and room labels at word level"],"may_wrap":["הערות prose, which is long and naturally multi-line","multi-word room labels such as אולם ספורט at spaces","teacher full names at spaces only in a notes-priority design"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [62, 110, 84, 89, 80, 294] · table 720×500px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 83, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [62, 110, 84, 89, 97, 277] · table 720×547px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 60, 60, 83, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r1A","good":"Compact 500px table with an even rhythm.
